items.title: High-regularity local developments for the selected matter sectors: vacuum with Lambda, scalar, strict barotropic fluid and geodesic dust
items.statement:
Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$ be constants, let $\Sigma$ be a smooth
three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and symmetric $2$-tensor $K$,
and suppose smooth matter initial data and a matter sector are given in one of
the following four branches, with the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] satisfied:

1. **vacuum with cosmological constant:** no matter fields; the constraints
   read $S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=0$;
2. **scalar field:** a model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ as in
   [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with smooth potential and initial data
   $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$;
3. **strict barotropic perfect fluid:** a model with smooth $p=p(\epsilon)$ and
   $\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$, with initial data
   $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]);
4. **geodesic dust:** a model $(\rho,u)$ as in [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]
   with initial data $(\rho_0,U_0)$, $\rho_0\ge0$ and $U_0$ a smooth
   future-directed unit timelike field on $\Sigma$.

Then in each branch there is a smooth local development with the properties
established in the corresponding item, [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]
(branch 2), [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]] (branch 3),
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] (branch 4) and, for branch 1, the vacuum
instance of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric
$g$ with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data $(h,K)$, solving
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ with the branch's stress tensor and matter
equations, with $\Sigma$ in the interior of its domain of dependence, and with
uniqueness near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

items.title: Local Cauchy development of the adopted Einstein field law for smooth constrained data in the selected matter sectors
items.statement:
Adopt the direct-equation presentation of the classical gravitational framework
for a model satisfying the spacetime and classical-domain postulate
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the field-and-matter postulate
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], with the field law
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]: on the matter domain of the model,
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab},\qquad \kappa=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4},$$
with $T$ the stress-energy tensor of the model's selected matter sector. Let the
sector be one of:

1. vacuum with cosmological constant ($T=0$);
2. the scalar-field model $(\varphi,V,K)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]
   with a chosen smooth potential whose scalar equation and stress tensor are
   those defined there;
3. the perfect-fluid model of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] with a
   smooth barotropic equation of state satisfying $\epsilon+p>0$ and
   $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ on the range of the data;
4. the dust model of [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]] with rest density $\rho\ge0$
   and prescribed smooth future unit velocity.

Let $(\Sigma,h,K)$ with the sector's smooth initial data (respectively nothing,
$(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$, $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$, $(\rho_0,U_0)$) satisfy the constraint
equations [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the sector's
stress tensor. Then the model admits a **local Cauchy development**: there are
a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of the framework and
a spacelike embedded image of $\Sigma$ inducing $(h,K)$ and the stated matter
data, solving the field law $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ and the
sector's matter equations on a neighborhood of $\Sigma$; $\Sigma$ lies in the
interior of its domain of dependence; and any two such developments of the same
data agree near $\Sigma$ up to an isometry fixing the data and the time
orientation. The development is local in time and no uniform-in-the-data
existence time or global statement is asserted.
items.physical_scope: Classical general relativity in the smooth high-regularity branch: four-dimensional smooth Lorentzian geometry of signature (-+++), cosmological constant Lambda, and one of the classical matter sectors — vacuum, a scalar field with smooth potential, a barotropic perfect fluid with 0<p'<1, or geodesic dust — with smooth constrained initial data; the conclusion is a local-in-time development before any flow crossing, and makes no statement about nature, no global or all-time existence, no non-smooth, boundary, shock or asymptotic regime, and no claim of optimal Sobolev threshold.

items.title: Scope and status of the Gr14 high-regularity symmetric hyperbolic material
items.statement:
This page contains the Gr14 high-regularity symmetric hyperbolic proof material:
the periodic first-order theory (E0), the harmonic-gauge reduced Einstein
equation and its subsidiary system (E1), the geometric data and local
development theorems (E2), and the selected matter reductions with the complete
geodesic-dust residual chain (E3, E3d--E3d.2). Its content is conditional:
the physical reading is the model deduction of
[[pthm-gr-high-regularity-local-development]] from the adopted postulates
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] and the matter definitions
[[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; the mathematical carriers are
[[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] and its prerequisites.

**What is established.** Local-in-time smooth developments of the adopted field
law with the selected matter sectors, from smooth constrained data, with
uniqueness near the initial surface up to a data-fixing time-orientation-
preserving isometry, and with the initial surface lying in the interior of its
domain of dependence.

**What is not established or assumed away.** No global or all-time existence,
no uniform existence time on noncompact data, no maximality or boundary
behaviour of the development (that is the scope of the successor page), no
shocks, free boundaries, vacuum boundaries or junction conditions, no
distributional or low-regularity sources, no optimal Sobolev threshold (the
theorem works in the smooth/high-regularity branch with $s\ge5$), no
quantitative measurement or observational claim. For dust, the construction
occurs before flow crossings and the velocity is prescribed separately, so
empty regions with $\rho=0$ are included and no division by $\rho$ occurs; the
density solves $\partial_sr=-r\chi$ with the explicit positive solution of
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]]. For the fluid branch the strict hypotheses
$\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'<1$ are essential; the failure at negative $p'$ is the
companion counterexample on the examples page. No statement is made that any
model here describes nature, and no empirical premise enters.

**Review flags recorded for the owner.** (i) The dust reduction's Schouten
normalization in the research design displayed the Kulkarni--Nomizu bracket
expression with a normalization that does not reproduce the
constant-curvature check under the stated Schouten tensor; the production items
fix the standard normalization explicitly and record the discrepancy in the
batch notes for independent review. (ii) The dust derivation uses Friedrich and
Rendall (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074) as provenance only, with all claims reproved
locally against the stated conventions; no literature authority substitutes for
a local argument.

items.title: Worked E0 check: constant-coefficient transport on the three-torus, explicit solution and conserved energy
items.statement:
On $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ take $m=1$, $A^0=1$, $A^1=2$, $A^2=A^3=0$, $B=0$,
so the system $(\star)$ of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]
reads $\partial_tu+2\partial_1u=0$, with $u_0\in H^s$ real-valued and $s\ge5$.
This example exhibits the explicit solution on the periodic domain,
$u(t,x)=u_0(x^1-2t,x^2,x^3)$, verifies that it is the E0 solution, and checks
the weighted energy identity $e'(t)=0$ for the energy
$e(t)=\int u(t)^2\,d\mu$ directly.

items.statement:
Take the barotropic equation of state $p(\epsilon)=\tfrac13\epsilon$ (so
